A first-time wellness visit is conducted for an 11-year-old male immigrant. His physical examination
reveals height in the 99th percentile with weight in the 50th percentile. Academic performance is poor,
and cognitive assessment indicates moderate mental disability. His vital signs show: temperature
98.9°F (37.5°C), blood pressure 102/80 mmHg, pulse 74/min, respirations 16/min, and oxygen
saturation 98% on room air. Laboratory findings are as follows: Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dL Hematocrit: 30%
MCV: 110 fL Leukocyte count: 5,500/mm^3 with normal differential Platelet count: 192,000/mm^3
Serum: Na+: 140 mEq/L Cl-: 101 mEq/L K+: 4.4 mEq/L HCO3-: 24 mEq/L BUN: 20 mg/dL Glucose: 90
mg/dL Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL Ca2+: 10.0 mg/dL AST: 12 U/L ALT: 10 U/L The patient is initiated on
vitamins B9 and B12. Which intervention would be most appropriate for managing this patient's
cardiovascular risk? Answer Choices: (A) Iron (B) Vitamin D (C) Riboflavin (D) Betaine
supplementation (E) Zinc supplementation (F) No interventions needed (G) Cysteine supplementation
(H) Pyridoxine (I) L-methionine therapy (J) Selenium supplementation
 A. Selenium supplementation
B. Zinc supplementation
C. No interventions needed
D. Pyridoxine
E. Betaine supplementation
F. Riboflavin
G. Vitamin D
H. Cysteine supplementation
I. Iron
J. L-methionine therapy
